details.label: Summary
details.text: Ongoing Mesoscale Convective Systems will continue to move southeast this evening. The airmass ahead of these storms remains very hot and unstable. A wind damage threat is expected to persist into the greater Washington D.C. area later this evening. As such, a new watch will likely be needed

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multiple southeast moving mesoscale convective systems (MCS) are ongoing across portions of northern/eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania. The leading MCS is currently located across the greater Pittsburgh area, with the trailing MCS across moving across northern Ohio and southern Lake Erie. Effective layer shear across these linear MCSs is characterized by 30-40 knots, which is more than sufficient to support ongoing organization as the clusters move southeast. Additionally, the airmass ahead of these storms remains very hot and humid, with surface temperatures in the 90Fs and dewpoints in the low-to-mid 70Fs. The result is steep low-level lapse rates and MUCAPE in excess of 3000 J/kg ahead of these storms, all the way into the greater Washington D.C. area. As evening progresses and the boundary layer cools, low-level lapse rates will weaken. However, the degree of thunderstorm organization and the very unstable environment ahead of the MCSs will maintain a threat for damaging wind well into the evening hours. A new watch will likely be needed to the southeast of ongoing watches across Pennsylvania, Ohio, and West Virginia

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: An organizing MCS will yield a greater risk for severe wind gusts across portions of southwestern Pennsylvania over the next 1-2 hours

details.label: Summary
details.text: An organizing MCS will yield a greater risk for severe wind gusts across portions of southwestern Pennsylvania over the next 1-2 hours

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Regional radar imagery depicts an organizing MCS across portions of western Pennsylvania, with volume scans over the past 30 minutes from KPBZ depicting embedded velocities up to 65 kts at 600 ft AGL. Numerous reports of wind damage have been noted with this complex, including downed trees and power lines, with a 62 mph wind gust also recently measured at KHLG in far northern West Virginia. The downstream environment remains favorable for damaging/severe wind gusts, with steep low-level lapse rates (7.5-8.0 K/km), moderately strong instability (2500-3000 J/kg MLCAPE), and around 30-40 kts of effective shear in place, as sampled by the 18z PIT observed sounding and recent objective analysis. Given this environment and the organizing MCS, a locally greater risk for damaging/severe wind gusts is likely to accompany this system as it progresses east-southeastward across portions of southwestern Pennsylvania
